findings.description: Spec text names three seemingly-independent triggers coordinated by an explicit anti-concurrency mechanism: 'republish after each successful event append and on demand, running republish and the periodic mark-refresh in one serialized loop, never concurrently.' All 3 A outputs (unanimously) read this as requiring real concurrency arbitration and built a tokio async runtime with a channel/select!-based single-consumer loop over 3 distinct trigger variants (AfterAppend, OnDemand, MarkRefreshTick) — modeling 'periodic mark-refresh' as an independently-fireable operation that could race with republish. All 3 B outputs (reconstructing from cycle.rs, tui_app.rs, republish.rs) show the real system has no such independent periodic-mark-refresh path and no concurrency to arbitrate at all: every trigger — post-append refresh (tui_app.rs run_form_action), manual [r], the hourly should_autorefresh check, TUI connect, and headless summary — invokes the identical synchronous fused sequence inside one function, `Publisher::republish_then_settle`: replay -> render tabs -> republish (write, under the advisory lock) -> settle/mark-refresh (read, unlocked) -> re-replay with settled marks. 'Never concurrently' cashes out (and is tested, in republish.rs's `every_settle_read_happens_after_all_writes_in_a_cycle`) as simple call-log ordering (every ReadPricePass index > every BatchUpdate index within a cycle) on a single thread — not as mutual exclusion between independently-scheduled operations. Mark-refresh is never triggered alone; it is inseparably fused to every republish call.

The advisory write-lock's scope is pinned identically by all 3 B outputs and modeled by none of A: `republish()` acquires the lock exactly ONCE (`lock.acquire()`), covering every tab's `batch_update_view` call plus the `set_tab_order` reassert, and releases it (scope-exit guard) BEFORE the settle/mark-refresh read begins — so mark-refresh always runs lock-free. Spec text never mentions a lock or its scope; all 3 A outputs substitute a channel-based single-consumer as the entire serialization mechanism and have no Lock concept at all.

Concrete, spec-silent failure/retry semantics unanimously pinned by B1/B2/B3, absent from all 3 A outputs: a single tab's `batch_update_view` failure flags ONLY that tab stale, writes a best-effort in-tab banner of exact text `"STALE — last sync {ts}"` (swallowing the banner write's own failure), and does not abort publishing the remaining tabs; a `set_tab_order` failure occurring AFTER every tab wrote successfully still forces the whole cycle's `published:false`; a held lock (another holder) causes a hard zero-write refusal — `published:false`, stale set unchanged, nothing written — rather than blocking or a partial write. A1/A2/A3 either swallow errors globally (`let _ =`) or invent unrelated backpressure policies (e.g. A3's capacity-1 coalescing channel) with no per-tab stale/banner/held-lock modeling.

The settle pass's bounded-retry mechanics are pinned identically by B1/B2/B3 and entirely absent from A: `SettleConfig::max_polls` defaults to 8; a still-transient symbol past the window degrades `TimedOut` (carrying its prior cached mark forward if one exists, else no mark); a terminal non-numeric reading degrades `Permanent` with no carry; and the canonical rounding site `price_to_cents` uses `round_half_to_even(price_usd × 100)` where a non-positive/sub-cent result degrades `SubCent` and a non-finite reading degrades `Permanent` — never a zero mark. A's `mark_refresh()`/`kernel.mark_refresh()` are opaque black-box calls with none of this detail.

Only B1 explicitly states that the settle pass is restricted to OPEN positions (`total_qty != 0` — matching `run_cycle_publishing`'s symbol filter in cycle.rs) and that closed/disposed symbols are never priced; B2 and B3 omit this. A single-run B finding, not corroborated across all 3 B runs, so weaker than the items above.

notes: A-direction agreement is high on the core architectural interpretation that drives finding #1 (tokio + channel + single-consumer loop + treating periodic mark-refresh as a distinct trigger) — all 3 runs converge there, each explicitly flagging it as an assumption. They diverge only on secondary, self-acknowledged-as-invented specifics (unbounded vs. capacity-1-coalescing channel, oneshot-reply vs fire-and-forget) that don't affect classification. B-direction agreement is high: all 3 reconstruct the same sequential republish-then-settle ordering (verified via call-log/index comparison), the lock-scoped-to-write-only design, per-tab stale+banner semantics with exact banner text, set_tab_order's published:false-on-failure rule, and max_polls=8 with the TimedOut/Permanent/SubCent taxonomy. Minor B asymmetries: B2 doesn't restate the offline-transport-error-propagation contract (present in cycle.rs's CycleError::View docs and captured by B1/B3), and only B1 states the open-positions-only settle filter explicitly.
